title: Polynomial translation modules are acyclic for internal lattice invariants
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. Let $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$ and put $A(S)=C(S,F)$ on the coherent profinite site, using all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For integers $r,m\geq0$ put $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ with its inverse-limit topology. Let $T_{r,m}$ be the internal direct sum of copies of $A$ on the monomials in $r+m$ variables $y_1,\ldots,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_m$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Give it the internal $A$-linear $L$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] determined by
$$(g\cdot f)(y,z)=f(y-g,z).$$
For a varying $g\in C(S,L)$ its coordinates are sections of $A(S)$ by $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset\mathbf Q_\ell\subset F$; the formula is polynomial substitution and extends to the internal direct sum. Work with ordinary internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and ordinary total right derived invariants [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] in compatible coefficient universes containing all profinite parameter sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Then
$$R^q\Gamma_{A,L}(T_{r,m})=0\qquad(q>0)$$
as internal $A$-modules, where $R^q\Gamma$ is the $q$th cohomology object of $R\Gamma(T_{r,m}[0])$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This includes $r=0$ and $m=0$. The module is the polynomial direct sum, without a degree bound, and $A_\Omega$ retains its noncomplete norm topology.

proof.text: Prove the assertion by induction on $r$, simultaneously for every $m\geq0$. If $r=0$, $L=1$ and the identity axiom forces every action to be trivial, so fixed sections and their inclusion are the identity functor and identity map. Its derived functor is again the identity; a module in degree zero has zero positive cohomology. This proves the base case for all polynomial spectator modules, including $m=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of polynomial translation acyclicity, rank-zero base case

proof.text: Suppose $r>0$ and the assertion holds for $r-1$ and every spectator count. Put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ for translation in $y_1$ and $G=\mathbf Z_\ell^{r-1}$ for translations in $y_2,\ldots,y_r$; reorder factors to write $L=G\times H$. For $n\geq0$ let $V_n$ be the finite-dimensional $E$-space of polynomials of total degree at most $n$ in all $r+m$ variables. Inclusions are injective, all translations preserve $V_n$, and $D_n=-\partial/\partial y_1$ satisfies $D_n^{n+1}=0$. The $G$-action commutes with $D_n$ since it substitutes only the other $y$ coordinates. In the monomial basis its matrix entries are polynomials in the $G$ coordinates, hence continuous. Finite Taylor expansion gives $\exp(tD_n)f=f(y_1-t,y_2,\ldots,z)$, so this is exactly the specified $H$-action. Thus the finite stages meet every algebraic and continuity hypothesis of [lem-sfb-ind-unipotent-procyclic-difference].

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of polynomial translation acyclicity, finite polynomial stages and nilpotent translation

proof.text: Each $M_n(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V_n)$ is the finite direct sum of copies of $A$ on its monomials: the coefficient projections and assembly are inverse continuous maps for the finite product topology. The colimit of these finite direct sums is the internal direct sum on all monomials, because a map out of either is precisely a compatible family of maps from its individual copies of $A$. These identifications intertwine the stage actions, so $\operatorname{colim}M_n=T_{r,m}$ as an action module. Apply [lem-sfb-ind-unipotent-procyclic-difference] with these stages, retaining the $G$-action. It gives $R\Gamma_H^G(T_{r,m}[0])\cong Q([T_{r,m}\xrightarrow{\Delta}T_{r,m}])$, where $\Delta f=f(y_1-1,y_2,\ldots,z)-f(y_1,y_2,\ldots,z)$. This is the asserted derived comparison for the whole sheaf colimit; no interchange of a derived functor with that colimit is inferred here.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of polynomial translation acyclicity, application of the rank-one analytic comparison

proof.text: Set $B=A[y_2,\ldots,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_m]$, the polynomial direct sum in the remaining variables. In $B[y_1]$ put $b_0=1$ and $b_n=(-1)^n y_1(y_1+1)\cdots(y_1+n-1)/n!$ for $n>0$. Their degrees are $n$ with invertible rational leading coefficients, so triangular elimination expresses each polynomial uniquely as a finite sum $\sum_n c_nb_n$, $c_n\in B$. Subtract the two products at $y_1-1$ and $y_1$: factoring their $n-1$ common factors gives $\Delta b_n=b_{n-1}$ for $n>0$, while $\Delta b_0=0$. Define $J(b_n)=b_{n+1}$ $B$-linearly, $p(f)=f(0)$, and $i:B\to B[y_1]$ by constants. Then $\Delta J=1$, $J\Delta=1-ip$, and $pi=1$. Every image of a monomial is finite, so all these formulas define internal maps of direct sums. They commute with the $G$-action, which acts on $B$ alone. Thus $i:B[0]\to[T_{r,m}\xrightarrow{\Delta}T_{r,m}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence in $\mathcal A_G(A)$, with inverse $p$ and homotopy $J$ in degree one. By step 3, $R\Gamma_H^G(T_{r,m}[0])\cong B[0]$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of polynomial translation acyclicity, explicit finite-difference contraction

proof.text: For the exact inflations from ordinary internal modules to $G$-action modules and then to $(G\times H)$-action modules, [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation] gives Grothendieck abelian categories, the specified right adjoints $\Gamma_G,\Gamma_H^G,\Gamma_{G\times H}$, and the conjugate equality $\Gamma_{G\times H}=\Gamma_G\Gamma_H^G$. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] to these two exact left adjoints and their composite. Its hypotheses are exactly those just stated, and it yields $R\Gamma_{G\times H}(T_{r,m}[0])\cong R\Gamma_G R\Gamma_H^G(T_{r,m}[0])$. By step 4 this is $R\Gamma_G(B[0])$. As a $G$-module $B$ is $T_{r-1,m}$, with the same $m$ spectator variables and translations in the remaining $r-1$ variables. The induction hypothesis therefore makes every positive cohomology object vanish. The induction proves the item for all $r,m$, for both choices of $F$.
